Formulation  
Patient is a middle-aged male presenting with depressive symptoms including low mood, decreased energy, poor sleep, decreased appetite, and reduced sex drive over approximately two months coinciding with starting a new job. Past medical history of hypothyroidism is relevant as it can contribute to fatigue and low mood. Family history of paternal suicide represents a background vulnerability. Physical symptoms including fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion may contribute or reflect an unrelated medical condition. No acute safety concerns. Protective factors include absence of suicidal ideation and stable marital support. Further assessment including physical examination and blood investigations are required to clarify medical contributors and guide treatment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Depressive symptoms with associated low energy, poor sleep, decreased appetite, and low mood  
- Patient Goal(s): Return to previous level of functioning and mood stability  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm or exclude medical contributors (e.g., thyroid function), assess severity of depression; initiate appropriate management if indicated  
- Actions (Patient): Book an in-person appointment with GP for examination and blood tests; monitor mood and energy; report any worsening or new symptoms promptly  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Conduct physical examination and order relevant investigations including thyroid function tests and full blood count; evaluate for depression; consider referral for mental health support or treatment per findings  

Secondary Problem: Fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve physical stamina and respiratory symptoms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify underlying cause of shortness of breath; address through medical management if indicated  
- Actions (Patient): Report any worsening breathlessness and functional limitations at GP visit  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Assess respiratory and cardiovascular status during examination; consider appropriate investigations and referrals  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Explanation of symptom association with depressive state and hypothyroidism; importance of medical assessment and investigations; encouragement to seek help if symptoms worsen  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased low mood, suicidal ideation, worsening fatigue or breathlessness  
- Coping Strategies: Not specifically recorded
